newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Edison, Centerior to merge in $4.8 billion deal.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Edison, Centerior to merge in $4.8 billion deal.

text.p: Electric utilities Ohio Edison Co. and Centerior Energy Corp. said Monday they agreed to merge, forming a new holding company, in a stock-for-stock deal valued at $4.8 billion.

The merger, which the utilities said they hoped to complete by the end of 1997, would create the nation's 11th largest investor-owned electric system. The deal comes amid a wave of consolidation in the increasingly competitive industry which faces regulatory and other changes.

Ohio Edison serves Akron and other parts of Ohio and its Pennsylvania Power Co. subsidiary, based in New Castle, Pa., operates in western Pennsylvania. Centerior Energy's Cleveland Electric Illuminating Co. and Toledo Edison Co. serve those areas.

"The combination of our contiguous service areas is a natural. Our service areas are located within a 500-mile radius of one-half of the U.S. population," said Robert Farling, chairman of Cleveland-based Centerior Energy.
Centerior Energy stock rose $1.625 to close at $9.25 on the New York Stock Exchange. Ohio Edison stock fell $1 to close at $19.75 on the NYSE.
The proposal drew mixed reaction from analysts.
"I'm not sure if it's positive for Ohio Edison because I think Ohio Edison takes on more financial risk by joining up with a weaker company," said Barry Abramson of Prudential Securities Research.
But McDonald & Co. analyst Nancy Benacci called it a "win-win" transaction for both companies.
"It really provides them with the right kind of combination to exist profitably in a deregulated environment," she said.
Under the definitive agreement, Ohio Edison shareholders will receive one share of the common stock of the new holding company, named FirstEnergy Corp., for each share of Ohio Edison stock held.
Centerior Energy shareholders will receive 0.525 share of FirstEnergy stock for each Centerior share.
The deal was valued at $4.8 billion based on Friday's closing prices.
As of June 30, the combined assets of Akron-based Ohio Edison and Centerior Energy were nearly $20 billion and annual revenues totaled $5 billion.
The companies said they anticipated the merger would add to earnings in the first year after the deal is completed and result in savings of $1 billion over the first 10 years.
They said they expected to cut 900 jobs from the companies' combined work force of about 11,000.
The companies said they intended to propose a plan to extend to Centerior's Cleveland Electric Illuminating Co. and Toledo Edison Co. customers a rate reduction program similar to Ohio Edison's.

The plan would call for a freeze of Clevelend Electric and Toledo Edison rates through 2005, a rate reduction of $300 million, or about 15 percent, in 2006, and accelerated depreciation of $2 billion in fixed costs during that period.

Ohio Edison and Centerior, with DQE Inc.'s Duquesne Light Co. in Pennsylvania, years ago formed a group to build and operate power generating plants, including four nuclear plants in Ohio and Pennsylvania.
If the merger is completed, FirstEnergy will have at least a majority stake in each of the nine coal and nuclear generating units and will have operational control of seven of the nine.
Willard Holland, president and chief executive officer of Ohio Edison, will become chairman of the board, president and chief executive officer of FirstEnergy.
Centerior's Farling will become vice chairman of FirstEnergy.
Ohio Edison and Centerior also said they expected FirstEnergy to set a goal of reducing debt by $2.5 billion through the year 2000.

The initial annual dividend on FirstEnergy's common stock is expected to be the same as Ohio Edison's annual dividend, currently $1.50 per share, and to provide Centerior holders with about the same dividend income they now receive on Centerior shares.
